title: TransferTraj: A Vehicle Trajectory Learning Model for Region and Task Trans

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract states 'It achieves an average improvement of 83.70% and 33.68% in zero-shot region transferability.' However, in Section 5.1 (Region transferability), the 33.68% improvement is explicitly attributed to the few-shot setting, not zero-shot: 'on the TP task, our method achieves improvements of 83.70% and 33.68% over SOTA models in zero-shot and few-shot settings.' The abstract incorrectly presents a few-shot result as a zero-shot improvement.

The paper states: 'In the zero-shot setting, only TP and OD TTE tasks are evaluated due to class space inconsistency issues for TR tasks, where varying road IDs prohibit direct cross-region transfer experiments.' However, the trajectory recovery (TR) task defined in the paper predicts GPS coordinates, not road IDs; the output space is continuous and thus no class space inconsistency exists that would inherently prevent zero-shot transfer. This reasoning contradicts the task formulation and is logically inconsistent.

Table 7 ('Efficiency of methods on TP task') lists numerical values under columns headed by dataset names and repeated sub-columns without any labels indicating what the numbers represent (e.g., model size in MB, training time in seconds/minutes, inference time). The table caption and surrounding text provide no units or definition, making the table uninterpretable and the efficiency claims unsupported.

predicted_errors.error_location: Trajectory Recovery (TR) task description in Section 5
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The TR task description introduces sampling parameters μ = 4·ε, 8·ε, and 16·ε, but the base quantity ε is never defined anywhere in the paper. The reader cannot ascertain what a value of ε corresponds to (e.g., base sampling interval, time step, or index count), leaving the experimental configuration ambiguous.
